questions.problem:
$1$ is **not** both even and odd.

Express the compound statement above in symbolic form given the following:

- $P:1\text{ is even}$

- $Q:1\text{ is odd}$
questions.worked_solution:
The given sentence is the negation of the following sentence: 

$1$ is both even and odd, 

which can be expressed symbolically as $P∧Q.$

The negation is represented by the symbol "$¬$". 

Therefore, the given sentence is expressed symbolically as $¬(P∧Q).$

questions.worked_solution:
Two negations in a row cancel each other out. So, we can simplify $¬(¬(P∧¬Q))$ to $P∧¬Q.$

Therefore, the given statement can be simplified to

$$
(P∧¬Q)∨P.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬P∨¬Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-4}} |
questions.worked_solution:
First, we add the columns for $¬P$ and $¬Q,$ 
where the truth values are opposite to the corresponding values in the columns for $P$ and $Q,$ respectively.

| $\,P\,$ | $\,¬P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Then, we add a column for $¬P∨¬Q.$ Remember that $¬P∨¬Q$ is true if either $¬P$ is true or $¬Q$ is true.

| $\,P\,$ | $\,¬P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬Q\,$ | $\,¬P∨¬Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬A∨B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |

| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-4}} |
questions.worked_solution:
First, we add a column for $¬A,$ where the truth values are opposite to the corresponding values in the column for $A.$ 

| $\,A\,$ | $\,¬A\,$ | $\,B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |

Then, we add a column for $¬A∨B.$ Remember that $¬A∨B$ is true if either $¬A$ is true or $B$ is true. 

| $\,A\,$ | $\,¬A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬A∨B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
